subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC success metrics (AtlasPayments)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@atlaspayments.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC success metrics (AtlasPayments)

Hi Danielle / Evan —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and a proposed baseline for the 4-week POC so we can lock timeline and owners. I pulled the items below from our conversation; please flag anything I mischaracterized.

Scope summary
- Integrate Redwood Inference for payments intent classification + fraud flag hints for two traffic slices (API-based requests from your gateway).
- Evaluation window: 4 calendar weeks (baseline bench + weekly readouts).

Proposed success criteria (gating signals)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 250 ms for single-turn requests (measured at our edge + your egress).
- Throughput: support sustained 500 req/s for peak 5-minute windows without degradation beyond latency SLO.
- Cost: productionized cost target <= $0.0009 per token (token accounting applied to request/response payloads).
- Quality: intent match (micro-F1) >= 92% on your labeled sample; false positive fraud-flag rate <= 1.5% when measured on the supplied holdout.
- Robustness: end-to-end accuracy drop <= 3% when traffic contains masked PII and shortened context (we'll test with your synthetic masked corpus).

Operational asks from AtlasPayments
- Provide ~10k representative anonymized request rows (CSV) that match the traffic mix you described (80% short payment auth, 20% long dispute notes).
- Provide a service account and a staging API endpoint for a limited test user set, or allow us to proxy a small percentage of live traffic (your choice).

Timeline (target)
- Week 0 (2027-08-02): kickoff + infra onboarding (keys, staging).
- Week 1: baseline run (synthetic + sampled traffic), initial readout.
- Week 2–3: iterative tuning + quality gates, integration validation.
- Week 4: acceptance run + final gating report.

Ownership
- Redwood sales: Ben Carter — commercial coordination, acceptance criteria owner.
- Redwood technical ops: Monica Patel — test harness, benchmarks, runbook.
- AtlasPayments: Danielle Park — data & stakeholder contact; Evan Liu (CTO) — tech approvals / SSO if needed.

Next steps (today)
1) Danielle: confirm alignment on the success metrics above and the timeline.
2) Danielle: share sample CSV or grant staging access by EOD Thu (2027-07-22) to keep kickoff on 2027-08-02.
3) Ben/Monica: produce POC playbook and a short load script; share Doc link.

Attachments: [Attachment: atlas-sample-traffic.csv (text/csv)], [Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Danielle Park <danielle@atlaspayments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@atlaspayments.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC success metrics (AtlasPayments)

Thanks Ben — this looks right and really helpful. A few clarifications before we sign off: 

- Traffic mix: yes, 80/20 split is accurate. For the long-form side we expect sequences up to ~3k characters (equates to ~600–700 tokens). The short auths are typically < 120 chars. Can you confirm the latency SLO is for the long-tail tests as well or we should treat those separately?

- Cost target: $0.0009/token sounds fine as a goal — can you confirm whether that assumes 8-bit quantization and any batching assumptions? We need realistic runway numbers for procurement.

- Data handling: we will share anonymized rows but want confirmation that Redwood will not persist PII and that logs are scoped to the POC and deleted on close. If you can send a short statement we can route to infra / security.

- Access: we prefer to provide a staging endpoint + service account rather than proxy live traffic during the POC. I will send the sample CSV by Wednesday.

If this is agreeable we can lock 2027-08-02 for kickoff.

Danielle Park
Head of Fraud & Risk | AtlasPayments
danielle@atlaspayments.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@atlaspayments.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC success metrics (AtlasPayments)

Hi Danielle — thanks for the questions, helpful. Quick answers and a couple of small edits to the plan below.

- Latency SLO scope: we'll measure both slices. For the long-form documents (up to ~700 tokens) we'll track a separate 95th percentile target and we'll mark that as a soft gate: long-doc 95th <= 650 ms (soft), short-turn 95th <= 250 ms (hard). That OK?

- Cost assumptions: the $0.0009/token goal assumes a quantized runtime (8-bit) plus continuous batching set to keep average latency within the SLO during steady-state. We'll include a line-item in the POC plan that models token counts, batching, and expected GPU minutes.

- Data handling: Redwood will not persist raw PII for the POC. Logs are collected for debugging only and will be deleted after the POC unless you request retention. I'll attach our short security statement and Monica will provide the minimal RBAC template.

- Access: great — staging endpoint works. Once you share the CSV we'll stage the baseline within 48 hours and run the first readout.

I've updated the POC playbook to reflect the long-doc soft gate and the cost assumptions. Link and attachments below. If that looks good we'll lock kickoff for 2027-08-02.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (application/pdf)], [Attachment: eval-harness-readme.md (text/markdown)]

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3742

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Danielle Park <danielle@atlaspayments.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC success metrics (AtlasPayments)

Thanks — I added a short ops checklist and owner map below to make the kickoff smoother.

POC ops checklist (Monica / Redwood ops)
- Receive sample CSV + confirm schema (expected columns: request_id, payload_text, labeled_intent, timestamp, traffic_slice).
- Provision staging service account and API key scoped to test project.
- Run baseline synthetic run (1000 short requests, 200 long documents) and publish latency/cost baseline within 48h of receiving data.
- Share eval harness (eval-harness-readme.md) and a load script for Atlas to run in their staging environment.
- Provide RBAC template & short security statement.

Atlas action items (Danielle)
- Share anonymized sample CSV (target: 10k rows) by Wed 2027-07-21.
- Confirm internal stakeholders for POC readouts (product, infra, procurement).
- Notify procurement of expected cost modeling (Ben will follow up with a simple cost estimate).

Acceptance measurement & artifacts
- We will provide a gating report with: token accounting, latency/throughput graphs, confusion matrix + F1, and regression notes with suggested prompts/tuning.

Operational notes
- If you want tighter privacy controls we can run in a customer-dedicated environment (Dedicated) but that will change lead times and cost — we can discuss if the POC shows good fit.

I’ll spin up the baseline scripts after I receive the CSV. Attaching the eval readme and a sample harness reference for your engineers.

Attachments: [Attachment: eval-harness-readme.md (text/markdown)]
